sentences.text: Social worker Priya Nair (S1) stated she spoke with Margaret Doyle (S2) on the phone on Monday.
Margaret Doyle (S2) described the home entrance as having a step that is 'a bit high'.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she feels cold and turned the heating on despite it being 'bitter' outside with wind from the fields.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she has nowhere to go and only has a quiz programme at four o'clock.
Margaret Doyle identified her GP as Dr Shah at Millbrook Surgery on Church Lane, noting Dr Patel retired last summer.
S2 stated she is happy for Kevin to join the rest of the assessment.
Kevin Doyle stated the house is too much for Margaret Doyle due to the stairs and garden.
Kevin Doyle suggested Margaret Doyle would be better off in a sheltered flat or a bungalow with a warden on site.
Margaret Doyle denied moving to a sheltered flat or bungalow, stating she has been over this topic.
Margaret Doyle stated she came to the house as a bride and Frank carried her over the step, and she does not want to go to a flat with strangers.
Margaret Doyle stated the house matters because it is her home where she brought the kids up, her garden is there, Frank's roses are there, Brenda lives next door, and she knows c.
Margaret Doyle stated she wants to stay in her own home for as long as she possibly can.
Kevin Doyle asked about selling the house and getting somewhere smaller.
Margaret Doyle stated she would not sell the house because she would not know where Biscuit (the dog) or Frank's roses would go.
Margaret Doyle stated it has been two years in August since Frank died from a heart attack, which was very sudden.
Social worker Priya Nair thanked Margaret Doyle for being honest and for the tea.
Social worker Priya Nair stated she would be fine regarding the wind.
Social worker Priya Nair advised Kevin Doyle to mind the step.
Margaret Doyle (S2) indicated she cannot manage 'big pans' but stated she can manage the kettle.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she does not trust herself to carry two cups and a frame.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she is left-handed and noted that breaking her 'good hand' makes everything harder.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated her wrist cast came off last Tuesday and she now wears a splint most of the time.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she has not done enough exercises for her wrist.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she uses a frame indoors most of the time, though she sometimes holds onto furniture instead because the frame gets caught on rugs and doorframes.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she has hardly been out since coming home, using Frank's old stick outside, and has only been out to the end of the path and to the doctor's once (with a
Margaret Doyle reported she is frightened of falling again.
Margaret Doyle stated she had three falls in the last six months: one in the garden before Christmas, one in the bathroom in January where she caught herself on the sink, and one '
Margaret Doyle stated she uses the upstairs toilet during the day and tries to limit afternoon drinking to reduce frequency.
Margaret Doyle reported she gets up once or twice at night to use the toilet and currently leaves the landing light on.
Margaret Doyle reported she has not had a proper bath since the January fall, stating she dares not get in because she cannot push herself up with her wrist and is worried about no
Margaret Doyle expressed she misses having a bath and feels she does not feel properly clean, especially her hair.
Margaret Doyle stated Brenda washed her hair over the kitchen sink last week, but she cannot keep asking her to do it.
Margaret Doyle reported dressing is very slow, taking forty minutes to an hour, and she sometimes sits down in between.
Margaret Doyle reported she cannot do the hooks on her bra and has been wearing the same cardigan most days because it is easier.
Margaret Doyle reported she has given up on wearing tights and now wears elasticated trousers.
Margaret Doyle reported she can get her slippers on but cannot put on shoes with laces.
Margaret Doyle reported she bought some velcro shoes by Kevin but found them a bit tight.
Margaret Doyle stated she sometimes does not get dressed and stays in her nightie, admitting she did this twice last week.
Margaret Doyle reported she goes down the stairs sideways or sometimes on her bottom if she is tired.
Margaret Doyle reported she goes up the stairs one at a time holding on with her right hand.
Margaret Doyle stated she leaves the bathroom frame at the bottom and holds on to the wall upstairs.
Margaret Doyle reported she has quite a few rugs in the hall and elsewhere.
Margaret Doyle stated some of the rugs were her late husband Frank's mother's and one was brought back from a holiday in Wales years ago.
Margaret Doyle reported Kevin is always on at her about the rugs.
Margaret Doyle stated she is past being embarrassed about personal care.
Margaret Doyle reported she does a strip wash at the sink upstairs using a flannel.
Margaret Doyle stated she uses the bath but not the shower.
Margaret Doyle stated she cannot do her hair with one hand.
Margaret Doyle reported she wears the same cardigan most days because it is easier.
Margaret Doyle stated she cannot do the hooks on her bra.
Margaret Doyle reported she has given up on tights and now wears elasticated trousers.
Margaret Doyle stated she can get her slippers on but cannot put on shoes with laces.
Margaret Doyle reported Kevin bought her some velcro shoes but found them a bit tight.
Margaret Doyle stated she sometimes does not get dressed and stays in her nightie, admitting she did this twice last week.
S2 disclosed that she sometimes does not make it to the toilet in time, resulting in leaking, particularly when rushing up the stairs.
S2 stated she wears pads at night, which she buys from the supermarket.
S2 reported that Kevin buys the pads for her in the big shop, though she noted she does not know what he thinks about this.
S2 expressed interest in seeing the continence service if it is free.
S2 stated she does not cook using the oven or hob since the fall.
S2 disclosed she cannot lift pans and stated she does not like being in the kitchen because that is where the fall happened.
S2 reported her clothes are hanging off her and she lost nearly a stone since Christmas.
S2 stated she weighed nine and a half stone all her married life and currently weighs eight stone something.
S2 reported her appetite comes and goes and she does not feel hungry like she used to.
S2 stated she eats toast with marmalade and tea for breakfast, soup (tomato or chicken) sometimes with bread for lunch, and occasionally yoghurt, crackers, and cheese for the night
S2 disclosed she finds it hard to cut cheese with one hand.
S2 stated Kevin does food shopping on a Sunday when he comes, and Brenda gets her milk and bread in the week if she runs out.
S2 reported she has a microwave and uses it to make jacket potatoes sometimes.
S2 disclosed Kevin put ready meals in the freezer but she cannot get the film off the top, stating she stabs it with a fork and it goes everywhere.
S2 stated she takes amlodipine (5mg once daily in the morning) and alendronic acid (70mg once a week on Monday).
S2 reported she takes paracetamol for her wrist, up to four times a day, but stated she does not take them that often.
S2 disclosed she found two paracetamol tablets still in the box last week (Tuesday morning and Thursday morning) and stated she does not know how she missed them.
S2 stated she sometimes has trouble opening the blister pack flaps and uses a butter knife.
S2 stated she has an alarm clock and could set it as a reminder for her medication.
S2 stated she has been forgetting her medication since the fall.
S2 stated she has been thinking about removing the rugs since about 2010.
Kevin Doyle stated the back step into the garden is a big drop and the light at the top of the stairs is on a pull cord she has to reach round for.
Margaret Doyle stated the house is warm enough now because the boiler is new, which Kevin sorted last year.
Kevin Doyle stated it took him three months to persuade Margaret Doyle to get a new boiler.
Margaret Doyle stated she used to walk to the lunch club as it was round the corner past the shops, but she cannot walk it now.
Margaret Doyle stated she would not want to walk in with the frame because everyone would be looking.
Margaret Doyle stated the house is very quiet.
Margaret Doyle stated she gets lonely.
Margaret Doyle stated some days she does not speak to anybody except Biscuit (the dog) and the man on the telly.
Margaret Doyle stated the days when nobody comes are long and very long.
Margaret Doyle stated she watches her programmes, does her word search (though she stated she cannot hold the pen now), and looks out the window.
Margaret Doyle stated after Frank died she was in a bad way, did not want to get up, and did not want to eat, sitting in his chair for weeks.
Margaret Doyle stated she saw Dr Patel (then Dr Shah) who put her on tablets for depression.
Margaret Doyle stated she saw a lady for bereavement through the surgery for six sessions, which she thought it was.
Margaret Doyle stated the lady helped and was very kind, letting her talk about Frank and not mind if she cried.
Margaret Doyle stated she came off the tablets (Sertraline) last spring.
Margaret Doyle stated Dr Patel said she could come off the tablets slowly, which she did.
Margaret Doyle stated she has not been taking Sertraline for over a year now because she did not like how they made her feel (flat).
Margaret Doyle stated her mood is up and down, but since the fall it has been more down than up.
Margaret Doyle stated she gets fed up and frustrated with herself and with her hand, but stated it is not like it was after Frank and not that black.
Margaret Doyle stated she still gets up, feeds Biscuit, and watches her programmes.
S1 summarised that since the fall on the third of March and two falls before that, S2 is finding it very hard to wash properly, especially bathing and hair washing, and getting to
S1 summarised that getting dressed takes up to an hour and wears S2 out.
S1 summarised that S2 is not able to prepare proper meals, is eating very little, and has lost nearly a stone.
S1 summarised that S2 has missed some of her tablets.
S1 summarised that S2 is on her own a lot, feels lonely, and is feeling more low than usual.
S1 stated that the above impacts have a significant effect on S2's wellbeing, physical health, safety, mood, and ability to see people.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she does not get the answers to her quiz programme but shouts at the telly.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she does not want to be put anywhere during the assessment.
Margaret Doyle stated she would like to have a bath again.
Margaret Doyle expressed she does not want to look like an old woman.
Margaret Doyle stated she would like a second rail and a second frame for upstairs.
Margaret Doyle stated she is interested in the assessment and has no objection to it.
Margaret Doyle reported she used to have a bath every night before bed with her radio on.
Margaret Doyle stated she is interested in the assessment and has no objection to it.
Margaret Doyle stated if she ever had to go into a home, she would want it to be Beechwood because Brenda's sister was there and they were lovely.
Margaret Doyle stated she is not there yet, not by a long chalk.
Margaret Doyle stated she would like to go back to the lunch club because she misses the people, specifically Joan and Pat who always sat together.
S2 stated that staying in her own home with her dog, Biscuit, is the most important thing for her.
S2 stated she wants to be able to have a proper bath and wash her hair.
S2 stated she wants to get back to the lunch club to see Joan and Pat.
S2 stated she wants to stop being frightened all the time of falling and of the kitchen.
S2 stated she would like to be able to cook herself a proper dinner now and then, such as mince and potatoes.
S3 reminded S2 about her roses.
S2 stated she wants to see her roses (which she identified as Frank's roses) come out this summer and be well enough to go out and look at them.
S2 stated she was dreading the assessment and thought S1 would come to take her away.
S1 stated she came to help S2 stay, noting that was the whole point.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she is happy for the social worker to share information with her GP and anyone involved in her support, adding 'mostly' when asked if she has anything to
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated the fall occurred on the third of March, a Monday, in the kitchen while she was going to make tea.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she does not know if she tripped or went dizzy, noting 'One minute I was at the sink and the next I was on the floor by the back door'.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she was on the floor for about two hours until it got dark.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Brenda (next door) found her because she noticed the curtains were not drawn and the kitchen light was not on, and Brenda let herself in with a key.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Brenda found her, rang the ambulance, and sat on the floor holding her hand until the ambulance arrived.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she could not call anyone herself because her phone was in the front room and she could not get to it, although she heard it ringing.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she kept talking to her cat, Biscuit, who came to sit with her.
Margaret Doyle (S2) denied banging her head, stating she did not bang her head and that the hospital checked and confirmed it was all the wrist.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she might have been 'a bit woozy' before the fall because she had not had much to eat that day.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she was admitted to St Aldhelm's hospital for four days.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she was admitted to the orthopaedic ward.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she had broken her left wrist, which was fractured.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated she had bruising on the side of her body ('black and blue down this side') but no broken hips.
Margaret Doyle admitted she did not tell her GP about the two earlier falls, noting she did not want to bother him.
Margaret Doyle reported she has not been referred to a falls service, though she noted there might be a pile of letters.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not wear a pendant alarm or any similar device around her neck.
Margaret Doyle stated she does not have a pendant alarm, noting Kevin mentioned it.
Margaret Doyle denied having any thoughts of harming herself or ending her life, stating she would not do it because she has too much to live for (her grandchildren and Biscuit).
Margaret Doyle stated even back then after Frank, she was very low but never thought of doing anything like harming herself or ending her life.
Margaret Doyle stated she would tell Dr Shah or Susan if things got very low again.
Margaret Doyle reported that her grandson, Jordan (Susan's son, age 22), has been borrowing her bank card to withdraw cash or obtain shopping items.
Margaret Doyle stated that bank statements showed withdrawals totaling approximately six hundred pounds over the last two months, which she claimed was more than she asked Jordan.
Margaret Doyle disclosed that she gave Jordan her bank card number and PIN when she first came out of hospital so he could do her shopping.
Margaret Doyle stated that Jordan still has her bank card and said he would bring it back on Saturday.
Kevin Doyle reported that his mother, Brenda, told him she thought she saw Jordan at a cash machine on the high street near the chemist, but noted she was not sure it was him as he
Kevin Doyle reported that he heard from one of Jordan's old mates' mothers that Jordan has gotten himself into debt with betting apps on his phone.
The social worker (Priya Nair) recorded Kevin's report about the betting debt as something said to Kevin, not as a confirmed fact.
Kevin Doyle stated that he thought they should ring the police because the situation sounds like theft.
Margaret Doyle denied wanting the police involved, stating she does not want them round the house for Jordan.
Margaret Doyle expressed the wish for Jordan to stop using her card and for her to get her card back.
The social worker explained that the information provided constitutes a safeguarding concern regarding someone taking money without permission.
Margaret Doyle confirmed she is happy for the social worker to share the information with the safeguarding team and for them to contact her.
S1 instructed that if S2 falls and is hurt or cannot get up, an ambulance should be called at 999.
S1 stated that Brenda knocking on the wall is really valuable for now and should be kept going.
S2 stated she would keep Brenda knocking on the wall.
S1 instructed S2 to keep her phone on her in her cardigan pocket, even when pottering, until the alarm is fitted.
S2 agreed to keep her phone in her pocket.
S3 stated he would ring S2 every night around eight o'clock.
S2 stated she did not have to have S3 ring her every night.
S3 stated he wanted to ring S2 every night because he wanted to.
Margaret Doyle (S2) stated Kevin Doyle (S3) is her son and is on an early shift, potentially arriving at half eleven.
S2 disclosed she manages her own money for bills and getting cash out, but stated she has been a bit short lately and is not sure where the money is going.
S2 stated she has been a bit short of money lately and is not sure where it is going, attributing it to not keeping track like she used to.
S3 stated he came straight from work and smelled of the warehouse.
Kevin Doyle stated he visits mainly on Sundays, does the big shop, sits with her for a bit, and sometimes midweek if he is on early shifts.
Kevin Doyle stated he lives in Northampton, it is forty minutes in the car, and he works shifts at a warehouse, making it hard to visit.
Kevin Doyle stated he has two teenagers and his wife works, so he does what he can.
Margaret Doyle stated Kevin does a lot and does more than he should.
Margaret Doyle stated her daughter Susan lives in Spain (Alicante), moved there with her husband eight years ago, and rings every week on Sunday nights, regular as clockwork, and来过
Margaret Doyle stated Susan wanted to come over when she had the fall but could not get time off.
Kevin Doyle stated Susan was on the phone to him every day though.
Margaret Doyle stated Susan was worried sick.
Margaret Doyle stated Brenda (next door) pops in most days, just for a minute.
Margaret Doyle stated Brenda knocks on the wall in the morning and she knocks back so Brenda knows she is alright, a practice they have done for years since Brenda's husband passed
Margaret Doyle stated Brenda is seventy-six herself with knees, so she cannot lean on her too much.
Margaret Doyle stated she used to go to the lunch club at St Michael's church hall every Wednesday.
Margaret Doyle described the lunch club as a proper dinner, cooked dinner, pudding, and then bingo or a quiz or someone talks about something.
Margaret Doyle stated there was a man last time with real owls in a box, and one sat on her arm.
Kevin Doyle stated Margaret talked about the owl for a month.
Margaret Doyle stated she had not been to the lunch club since the fall.
Margaret Doyle stated the lunch club is now on Thursdays at twelve o'clock because they moved it when the new vicar came.
Margaret Doyle stated she never drinks alcohol, Frank liked his pint of bitter at the club but she never touched it because she cannot stand the smell.
S2 stated her income consists of her state pension and Frank's railway pension, from which she receives half as a widow's pension.
S2 stated they own the house, which was paid off years ago, noting that Frank was very proud of it.
S2 stated there is approximately nine thousand pounds in a building society account, which she described as funeral money and a bit for the grandchildren.
S2 denied receiving Attendance Allowance, stating she did not think she was getting it.
S3 stated that nobody had ever told them about the Attendance Allowance benefit.
S1 explained that a financial assessment would be required if the council arranged ongoing care, noting that the house is not counted for care at home.
S2 expressed a preference to pay a contribution to stay in her own home rather than move elsewhere.
The social worker offered to find out about transport options like a volunteer driver or minibus for the lunch club.
Margaret Doyle stated she would like the social worker to find out about transport for the lunch club.
Kevin Doyle agreed to take his mother to the Midshire building society branch on Friday morning to cancel the card and order a new one.
The social worker confirmed she would make a referral to the safeguarding team today before finishing the afternoon.
S1 stated it is likely S2 will meet eligibility criteria for support, noting this is a recommendation that must be agreed upon.
S1 proposed a request for reablement, described as short-term, usually free for up to six weeks, with carers coming in to help S2 get her confidence back.
S1 proposed a plan for reablement involving a morning visit to help with washing, dressing, and tablets, and a teatime visit to help with a meal.
S1 stated the proposed reablement plan would start every day and taper off as S2 gets more confident, noting this was not yet agreed.
S1 stated she would need to put the reablement request in and get manager approval, promising to let S2 know by the end of next week.
S3 stated the reablement request was not definite.
S2 stated she did not want someone bossing her about in her own kitchen.
S1 agreed to include the request for 'no bossy carers'.
S1 planned to refer S2 to occupational therapy today for a bath lift, board, second rail on stairs, second frame for upstairs, and an assessment of the back step and pull cord.
S1 stated the OT waiting list is about three weeks and she would mark the referral as a priority due to falls, but could not promise it would be quicker.
S1 planned to make a safeguarding referral about the card this afternoon.
S1 planned to refer S2 for a Careline telecare alarm (a watch that can detect a fall), noting they usually fit it within about ten days.
S2 identified the telecare device as 'the Carolyn'.
S1 planned to write to Dr Shah regarding a referral to the falls clinic and to mention weight loss, continence issues, and missed tablets.
S1 planned to ring the chemist on Station Road about a pack of tablets that is easier to open.
S2 corrected S1, stating her doctor is Dr Shah, not Dr Patel.
S1 planned to put in the request for reablement (morning and teatime visits) and let S2 know the outcome by the end of next week.
S1 planned to find out about transport to the lunch club at St Michael's on Thursdays and let S2 know what is available.
S1 instructed S3 to take S2 to the Midshire branch on Friday morning to cancel the card and get a new one.
S3 confirmed he would take S2 to the Midshire branch on Friday morning.
S1 instructed S3 to help S2 fill in the Attendance Allowance form, which S1 would post out along with the financial assessment form.
S3 stated he would do the forms on Sunday with S2.
S2 stated S3 would take the rug up in the hall this weekend, specifying only the hall rug, not the one in the room.
S2 stated she would set her alarm clock for nine o'clock for her morning tablets.
S1 planned to ring S2 on Monday to check how Friday went at the building society and to check in.
S1 planned to come back and see S2 again on Tuesday the fifteenth of April at about two o'clock.
S3 stated he would try to be there for the appointment on Tuesday the fifteenth and would swap a shift.
Kevin Doyle agreed to see the social worker again on the fifteenth.
